Arasan, the chess engine Gambit plays (its computer players, its coach and the review of a finished game), built from
source as a single-threaded WebAssembly module, with its neural network.

Source:   https://github.com/jdart1/arasan-chess, commit 84a67879b4b6c03fe5e2773ff22b9ceab1982375 (1 November 2026,
          version 26.1), by Jon Dart
Changes:  arasan-wasi.patch, applied to that commit: no thread is started (the search runs on the caller's own, so a
          "go" runs to its end inside the call and every search needs a limit), the UCI loop takes its commands one at
          a time from the page's worker instead of standard input (new file src/wasm.cpp, which replaces arasanx.cpp's
          main()), the network is not read from a file: the worker asks the engine for room (net_alloc), copies the
          .nnue file's bytes in and calls net_ready, which reads it and gives the room back; no book, no ECO file, no
          tablebases (the Fathom code is a submodule that is not fetched), the five `throw` statements of the sources
          the build uses stop the engine instead (the build has no exceptions; none is ever thrown), "go nodes N" is new
          (the search ends at the first count of positions past N, once its first iteration is whole: Gambit's levels
          are set by positions, not time), MultiPV allows up to 16 lines (10 before), bitboards use WebAssembly's native
          64-bit integers. No rule, search or evaluation is changed. wasi-shim/ stands in for what a WebAssembly C++
          library leaves out: <thread>, <mutex>, <condition_variable> and <pthread.h> (nothing is ever started),
          <fstream> (a file that can't be opened), and <immintrin.h>, the ~50 x86 SSE instructions the network code uses,
          written over WebAssembly SIMD with the same arithmetic. WebAssembly SIMD needs Safari 16.4 / iOS 16.4 or later.
Build:    build.sh (clang 18 for wasm32-wasi, with the WASI C library and libc++ from Ubuntu's wasi-libc and
          libc++-18-dev-wasm32 packages; the C++ library and the C library are linked into the .wasm, under the
          Apache 2.0 licence with the LLVM exception and the MIT and public-domain terms of wasi-libc, none of which
          asks for more than they already get from being named here). The script writes arasan.wasm and arasan.nnue.z.
          arasan.wasm: SHA-256 da4cfbf4aa0d3853b52d70d8220539483e0ef656d6a283a3c197dd4ae8ec02c6, 840,050 bytes.
Network:  arasanv9-20261023.nnue, from network/ in the same commit, 28,456,512 bytes, SHA-256
          95d981f4e03598a3110484c69f145455c278a525c62acd2a30c26f953382078c: 9 king buckets x 768 features into 1,536
          int16 neurons per side, then a sparse 1536 -> 16 -> 32 -> 1 head in int8 and int32, 8 variants by piece count.
          Trained by the author with his fork of the bullet trainer (his README); what positions this version was trained
          on is not stated (an earlier network's change log says "6B+ lc0 + selfplay games"). arasan.nnue.z is that file
          deflated raw by pack-net.mjs (13.3 MB; SHA-256 43f55bca0cc895a8319b7162f5e3fbac98e008ff661fdc0ee17c4f734bb85b3b),
          and unpacked by fillNet() in gambit-arasan.js into the engine's memory byte for byte (tests/gambit-engine.mjs
          checks the search it then plays, which any changed byte would move).
Licence:  Arasan: MIT, Copyright 1994-2026 by Jon Dart, and its LICENSE grants the same terms to "the contents of the src,
          book, doc, prj, tests, and network directories", so the network is under it too (the engine's own repository
          carries it, with no separate licence for it). Its text is LICENSE-Arasan.txt, and is here:

          Not taken from the repository: its opening book (book/, 33 MB), the Windows GUI (and the piece pictures and
          lunasvg it uses), the opening names (chess-openings, CC0), the Fathom tablebase code and the utilities.

Why not the Caissa this replaced: its network (Caissa-Nets) carries no licence file, though the engine is MIT
(docs/licences-images-and-engines.md). Why not the Stockfish before it: GPL v3. Arasan is the weaker of the engines that are
clean (Korbi, 3 November 2026: "yea we go for the weaker one"): about 2.5 times the time per position of Caissa's in
WebAssembly, and weaker at the same count of positions (tools/engine-levels-gambit-arasan.jsonl).
